solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Burning desire of dad to collar younger Arab

indicators.note: to collar someone is to grab them round the neck, so one piece wraps around the rest

parts.note: Pa is an informal word for a father
yr is the standard abbreviation of younger
someone from Oman is an Arab

explanation.surface: A father grabs a younger Arab man by the collar, apparently in the grip of some burning desire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burning desire' reads as a figure of speech but is meant literally: an urge to set fires. YR is a standard abbreviation solvers may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyromania is the compulsive urge to start fires, which is literally a craving for things to be set alight.

clue.text: New spade alone maybe with power to pull up tree

indicators.note: in a down clue, pulling something up makes it read from the bottom to the top

parts.note: N is the standard abbreviation for new
an ace is a single pip on a card, so the ace of spades is a spade alone, as an example
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A gardener wonders whether a new spade on its own, or with a power tool, can uproot a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: N, ACE and P are strung together and then read upwards to give PECAN. 'Spade alone' is a card with one spade on it, the ace of spades.
explanation.definitionFit: The pecan is a North American hickory species grown for its edible nuts, so it is one particular kind of tree.

clue.text: Tear around neighbourhood, nearly causing prang

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
around means surrounding, so one word goes on either side of another

parts.note: to rend is to tear apart
an area is a neighbourhood; without its last letter it gives these three letters

explanation.surface: Someone tearing around the local streets very nearly has a car crash.
explanation.walkthrough: AREA loses its last letter and sits inside REND. A prang is British slang for a minor car crash, and to rear-end another car is to drive into its back.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a minor road accident; rear-ending means driving into the back of another vehicle, a typical small collision.

clue.text: Say nothing of parent's promise to pen article

indicators.note: to pen is to shut in an enclosure, so one piece is enclosed by others

parts.note: a mum is a parent, here with the possessive
the definite article
to give your word is to promise

explanation.surface: A parent promises to write an article but asks that nobody talk about it yet.
explanation.walkthrough: Mum is the British word for mother, and 'mum' on its own also means silent, which is why the idiom works.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is an instruction to keep a secret, meaning keep quiet and tell nobody.

clue.text: Country never without king or queen

indicators.note: without can mean outside, so one piece is placed outside another

parts.note: no way means never, not a chance
R abbreviates both rex (king) and regina (queen)

explanation.surface: A country that has never been without a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like lacking, but it means outside. Fittingly, the answer is itself a monarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway is a Scandinavian nation, one example of a sovereign state.

clue.text: Utterly disorganised prince turning back on elegance

indicators.note: turning back means heading the opposite way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a rana is a Hindu prince in India and Nepal
chic is stylish elegance

explanation.surface: A chaotic prince abandons his stylish ways.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' means placed above. A rana is a crossword favourite for an Indian prince.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchic describes a state with no order or control at all, which is complete chaos.

clue.text: In US law officer, it reflects rank

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: a fed is an American federal agent, such as an FBI officer

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror is back to front, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: An American police officer thinks about their rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like a position in the police hierarchy; here it is the adjective meaning foul-smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives mean having a strong offensive smell, so they are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Passing fancy female, attorney spun around

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female

indicators.note: spinning something round makes it face the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney in the US

explanation.surface: A lawyer briefly takes a fancy to a woman and is spun around.
explanation.walkthrough: F is followed by DA turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A fad is a short-lived craze or enthusiasm, something people like briefly before moving on.

clue.text: Failing to conceal bottom, one's skimpy costume

indicators.note: hiding the bottom of a down entry means its lowest, final letter disappears

parts.note: tanking is informal for failing badly; its last letter is dropped
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A swimsuit so skimpy it fails to cover the wearer's bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about a bottom that is not covered; really the bottom letter of TANKING is removed. A tankini is a swimsuit with a tank top and bikini bottoms.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a two-piece swimming outfit, a bathing costume that exposes more skin than a one-piece.

clue.text: Group of players without a match?

definitions.text: Group of players without a match?

parts.words: Group of players without a match?
parts.note: surface reading: a sports side with no fixture arranged
setter's reading: a side with no equal anywhere, unbeatable

explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' suggests a game, but the setter means an equal: a side so good nothing matches it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names an ideal line-up of the best possible performers, which would be unrivalled.

clue.text: Archbishop, returning bow note, waves to Richelieu

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: a bow is a curve or arc
n. is a dictionary abbreviation for note
Richelieu was French, and mer is French for sea, the waves

explanation.surface: An archbishop returns a bow and a note and waves to Cardinal Richelieu, a meeting of churchmen.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets up a churchman greeting a French cardinal; 'waves' is in fact the sea, in French. Thomas Cranmer was Archbishop of Canterbury under Henry VIII.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Cranmer led the English church as Canterbury's senior bishop during the Reformation, so he is a specific holder of that title.

clue.text: Not only post, presumably, that's slow

parts.note: not only X, but Y is X and Y
post is Latin for after; its natural partner is ante, Latin for before

explanation.surface: Complaining that the post is slow, and not only the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' looks like the mail, but it is the Latin prefix; post and ante go together, so 'not only post' means 'and ante' as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is the Italian musical direction for a moderately unhurried, walking pace.

clue.text: For speaking out, dissenting voice is called before the union

indicators.note: speaking something out means saying it, so we go by how a word sounds

parts.note: nay is a vote against, a dissenting voice

explanation.surface: At a union meeting, a dissenting voice is called to speak out before the vote.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'union' looks like a trade union, but it is marriage. Née introduces a woman's maiden name.
explanation.definitionFit: Née, French for born, introduces the surname a woman had before marrying, i.e. her name prior to the wedding.

clue.text: It's the march forming a line to the right

indicators.note: forming means shaping something new, so the letters are rearranged into a new word

parts.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: Protesters form a line and march off to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' suggests marchers in formation, but it is a political line. Thatcherism is the free-market politics of Margaret Thatcher, British Prime Minister 1979-90.
explanation.definitionFit: A political line is a policy position, and Thatcherism was a right-wing, conservative doctrine.

clue.text: Put in — or put up — pleasing dispatch in chair?

definitions.note: verb phrase; the question mark flags a definition by example

parts.note: to elect is to vote into office

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round
cute means attractive, pleasing

explanation.surface: A pleasing speech from the chair after someone is voted in, or proposed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a committee chair and a nice dispatch; 'chair' is the electric chair and 'dispatch' means kill.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispatch is to kill, and the electric chair executes a condemned prisoner with a lethal current.

clue.text: Graft, to acquire spending money

parts.note: to bud a plant is to graft a bud onto it
to get is to acquire

explanation.surface: Working hard in order to earn some spending money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Graft' looks like the British slang for hard work, but it is the gardening sense of grafting.
explanation.definitionFit: A budget is the sum of cash allotted for outlays over a period.

clue.text: Bubble, say, flying low after delivery

indicators.note: things sent flying are scattered in all directions, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: A bubble drifting along close to the ground after being released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example', but it is part of the letters to rearrange. 'Delivery' is childbirth, not a parcel.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the brief tearful depression many mothers feel in the days after giving birth.

clue.text: Fifty-one assigned to cat? Over forty fewer?

definitions.note: a cryptic hint at a cat's nine lives, not a synonym

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
a feline is a cat

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a cat has fifty-one lives and is told no, over forty fewer.
explanation.walkthrough: A cat has nine lives, more than forty fewer than fifty-one, so the second sentence plays on lives; the answer is the line of the palm said to show how long one lives.
explanation.definitionFit: In palmistry the life line is read for length of life, and a cat is traditionally granted nine lives.

clue.text: On returning, wasn't keeping a single tool

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so everything reads backwards
keeping something means holding on to it, so one piece holds another

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
a single is one

explanation.surface: On the way back, someone realised they hadn't kept a single tool.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal applies to the whole assembled string, after the insertion; the apostrophe is ignored. A tenon is the tongue of a woodworking joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon saw is a small stiff-backed handsaw used by joiners for cutting precise joints.

clue.text: Gave advice from a fan of marriage? Only the one time

indicators.note: keeping only one where there are two means a duplicate is removed

parts.words: advice from a fan of marriage
parts.note: a fan of marriage would advise 'best to wed'
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone keen on marriage gives advice: do it, but only once.
explanation.walkthrough: BEST TO WED has two Ts together; keeping only one gives the answer. The surface reads as advice to marry only once.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestow is to present something as a gift or honour, so the past tense matches handed over.

clue.text: Part of state visit of queen maybe mostly to streets

indicators.note: mostly means not all, so the last letter is lost
to visit a place is to go inside it, so one piece enters another

parts.note: St is short for street, so STS is streets
a queen is a female cat, so a kitty perhaps; without its last letter

explanation.surface: A state visit by the Queen includes a tour of the streets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' looks royal, but a queen is a female cat. St Kitts is one of the two islands of the Caribbean state of St Kitts and Nevis.
explanation.definitionFit: The federation of Saint Kitts and Nevis has two islands, so each one is a component of that country.

clue.text: High Court writ dismissing case stops a corporation

indicators.note: a case is the outside of something, so dismissing it strips the outer letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a corporation is an old jocular word for a pot belly, a tum
writ with its outer letters removed

explanation.surface: A High Court writ is thrown out, which stops a corporation in its tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: The legal surface misleads twice: 'case' is the outer letters and 'corporation' is an old jokey word for a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium is a tall open central hall or courtyard in a building, often several storeys high.

clue.text: One's going to miss tracking European criminal

parts.note: I'll means I will, i.e. one is going to
E is the abbreviation for European
a gal is a girl, a miss

explanation.surface: Someone about to lose track of a European criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a verb but is a young woman, and 'tracking' means following behind the European.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe something against the law, forbidden by statute.

clue.text: Obstruct, confine or stifle

parts.note: to dam a river is to obstruct it
to pen animals is to confine them

explanation.surface: Three near-synonyms for holding something back, listed as alternatives.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like a list of three synonyms, but the first two are joined to make the answer and the last is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To dampen enthusiasm or a fire is to suppress or muffle it, which matches smothering it.

clue.text: Book date with PTA for arranging simple course

indicators.note: arranging means putting in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written; with adds these letters

explanation.surface: Booking a date with the parent-teacher association to arrange a simple course of study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' suggests a course of lessons, fitting the school surface; it is a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A jacket spud cooked in the oven makes an unfussy dish, one plain part of a meal.

clue.text: Canon listing all works primarily

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only the opening letter of each word is kept

parts.note: the first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A literary canon mainly lists all of an author's works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canon' suggests a list of approved writings, fitting the surface; it is used in its sense of rule.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a rule or principle, especially a church decree, so it is a synonym for a rule laid down.

clue.text: Whiskey and fish deliveries one on strike couldn't touch

definitions.text: deliveries one on strike couldn't touch

parts.note: W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ides is a variant of ide, a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Whisky and fish being delivered to a picket line that striking workers refuse to touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On strike' suggests industrial action, but it is the cricket batter facing the bowling. In cricket a wide is a ball bowled out of the batter's reach, and it gives the batting side a run.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide is a cricket ball bowled too far from the batter to be hit, so it is out of range.

clue.text: Tips for improvements

definitions.meaning: first meaning: turns something upside down, as a verb
second meaning: upward changes, as in business, as a noun

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips' looks like hints or advice for getting better, but it is the verb meaning overturns.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb meaning overturns and as a plural noun meaning upswings in fortune.

clue.text: Little hope of end to downpour, indeed!

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of downpour
ay is an old word for yes, indeed

explanation.surface: Little hope of the rain stopping, indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a gloomy weather remark; the idiom 'a ray of hope' supplies the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ray of hope is a faint glimmer of optimism, so the word alone suggests only a slight chance.

clue.text: Quiet bore gets promoted

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quiet
bore is the past of bear, to carry, and lugged means carried

explanation.surface: A quiet, dull person somehow wins promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a tedious person, but it is the past tense of bear, meaning carried.
explanation.definitionFit: To plug a product is to publicise it enthusiastically, so both words mean advertised.

clue.text: Fresh case of Sauternes to have in for one

indicators.note: to have something in is to hold it inside, so one piece contains another

parts.note: say means for example, as does for one

indicators.note: a case is the outer shell, so only the outside letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of Sauternes

explanation.surface: Getting in a fresh case of Sauternes, a sweet French dessert wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' looks like new stock, but it means cheeky. SAY takes in SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh can mean impudent or cheeky, and sassy describes someone lively and cheekily bold.

clue.text: Carol's bloke on lookout from place his young lady might be picked up?

indicators.note: to pick something up is to catch it by ear, so we go by how the words sound

parts.words: from place his young lady might be
parts.note: whence means from which place, and a lass is a young lady

explanation.surface: A man on lookout at the place where his girlfriend might be collected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' is not a woman but the Christmas carol 'Good King Wenceslas', whose king 'looked out' on the feast of Stephen. The sound match is approximate.
explanation.definitionFit: In the familiar Christmas song the good king looks out of his window, so he is the song's watching man.
